title: Clothing and shopping
goal: By the end of this lesson you can name everyday and winter clothing, describe what people wear, point at items with ce / cette / ces, and handle a shopping conversation in a Quebec store, including Quebec words like tuque, mitaines, bas and chandail.

body: Learn each item with its article: *le pantalon* (pants, singular in French!), *le jean / les jeans*, *la chemise* (shirt), *le t-shirt*, *la robe* (dress), *la jupe* (skirt), *le manteau* (coat), *la veste* (jacket), *les bottes* (boots).
Quebec has its own everyday words: *le chandail* (sweater or top), *les souliers* (shoes), *les bas* (socks), *le foulard* (scarf), *le coton ouaté* (hoodie, sweatshirt).
learn.tip: In France, 'bas' means stockings and 'mitaines' are fingerless gloves: in Quebec they're socks and mittens.

body: *Porter* = to wear (a state): *Elle porte une robe rouge.* *Mettre* = to put on (an action): *Mets ta tuque!* *S'habiller* = to get dressed. *Enlever* = to take off: *Enlève tes bottes.*
Colours and adjectives go after the noun and agree: *une tuque noire*, *des bas blancs*, *un manteau chaud*. Remember *beau / belle* goes before: *un beau chandail*.

learn.h: This, that, these: ce, cet, cette, ces
body: To point at things in a store, use demonstrative adjectives: *ce* (masculine), *cet* (masculine before a vowel), *cette* (feminine), *ces* (plural).
Add *-ci* (this here) or *-là* (that there) to contrast: *ce chandail-ci ou ce chandail-là?* In Quebec speech, *-là* is used constantly: *C'te chandail-là.*
learn.tip: Ce, cet, cette all sound almost the same in speech: [sè(t)].

body: *Je cherche un manteau.* (I'm looking for a coat.) *Vous avez ça en noir?* *Quelle taille?* (What size?) *Je porte du medium / du dix.* *Je peux essayer ce chandail?* (Can I try on this sweater?) *Où sont les cabines d'essayage?*
*Combien ça coûte?* / *C'est combien?* *C'est en solde.* (It's on sale.) *Je vais le prendre.* (I'll take it.) At the cash: *Comptant ou carte?* (Cash or card?)

Remember *magasiner* (to go shopping) from lesson 33. Winter shopping means *une tuque*, *des mitaines*, *des bottes d'hiver* and *un habit de neige* (snowsuit). Stores announce *les soldes de l'après-Noël* and *le Vendredi fou* (Black Friday).

quebec.intro: Quebec clothing words differ from France in ways that can confuse: bas are socks, mitaines are mittens, a chandail is a sweater, and a tuque is the winter hat everyone owns.

items.note: neutral in Quebec, used by everyone

dialogue.fr: Oui, je cherche un manteau d'hiver et une tuque.
dialogue.en: Yes, I'm looking for a winter coat and a toque.

dialogue.fr: Je porte du medium. Vous avez ce manteau-là en noir?
dialogue.en: I wear a medium. Do you have that coat in black?

dialogue.fr: Oui. Les cabines d'essayage sont au fond. Et les tuques sont en solde, vingt pour cent.
dialogue.en: Yes. The fitting rooms are at the back. And the toques are on sale, twenty percent off.

dialogue.fr: Parfait. Je vais prendre le manteau et cette tuque grise.
dialogue.en: Perfect. I'll take the coat and this grey toque.

dialogue.fr: Ça fait deux cent dix dollars. Comptant ou carte?
dialogue.en: That's two hundred ten dollars. Cash or card?

speak.prompt: Describe what you are wearing today, with colours.
speak.model: Aujourd'hui, je porte un jean bleu, un chandail gris et des souliers noirs.

speak.prompt: You're in a store: ask for a size, a colour and the price.
speak.model: Vous avez ce chandail en medium? En rouge? C'est combien?

speak.prompt: Tell a child what to put on before going out in winter.
speak.model: Mets ton manteau, ta tuque, tes mitaines et tes bottes. Il fait frette!

write.prompt: Write 6 sentences about a shopping trip: what you looked for, tried on, bought and paid.
write.model: Samedi, je suis allé magasiner au centre-ville. J'ai cherché des bottes d'hiver. J'ai essayé trois paires. J'ai choisi des bottes noires très chaudes. J'ai aussi acheté des bas de laine et une tuque. Tout est en solde cette semaine, alors j'ai payé seulement cent vingt dollars.
